advisory.finding: /health now performs a synchronous Gerrit auth network call on every request (check_auth with a 5s socket timeout), but autodeploy's drain probe curls /health with -m INFLIGHT_TIMEOUT (default 5s). When Gerrit is slow/unreachable, /health latency approaches or exceeds 5s, so bot_in_flight_reviews() times out and returns -1 (in_flight unreadable), causing the deploy to run WITHOUT the drain check and kill in-flight reviews — the exact regression the drain contract exists to prevent.
merged_from: The post-deploy readiness gate curls /health with `-m 3`, but the new auth probe can make /health take up to ~5s when Gerrit auth is slow/unreachable. A newly-deployed, process-healthy bot whose only problem is degraded Gerrit auth (or transient Gerrit latency) will fail the readiness curl and be rolled back.
scenarios: Gerrit REST is degraded/slow while a review is in flight; the review-bot's /health blocks ~5s on the auth probe; autodeploy's 5s in-flight curl times out and the deploy proceeds blind, killing the review invisibly.

evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py:132-134: `check_auth` calls `self._request("GET", "/a/accounts/self", timeout=5)` and only raises via _request's HTTPError/URLError paths.
gerrit_client.py:122: `with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:` — default opener follows redirects, so a 3xx→200 login page is not a GerritError.
check_auth never inspects the response body or asserts it is the expected account JSON, so 'checked and authed' is indistinguishable from 'redirected to an anonymous 200'.
advisory.finding: check_auth treats any non-raising _request as authenticated success, but urllib.request.urlopen follows 3xx redirects by default; a Gerrit misconfiguration that redirects /a/accounts/self to an anonymous login page returning 200 would pass check_auth even though the bot is NOT authenticated — the auth oracle can report 'authed' when it never truly verified identity.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have check_auth capture (status, text) and verify status==200 and that _strip_xssi(text) parses to an object containing the bot's account id, rather than trusting the absence of an exception.
